newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan land auction price higher than expected.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan land auction price higher than expected.

text.p: Taiwan's finance ministry said on Thursday its Wednesday auction on 10 pieces of state land went smoothly, with bidding prices much higher than the base prices.
"The auction results surprised us, with bidding prices roughly double the base prices," a ministry official told Reuters.
Three of the 10 pieces of state land, located in the capital Taipei's expensive commercial districts, attracted most attention, he said by telephone.

The winning bidding prices for the three pieces of land were T$292 million, T$237 million and T$220 million, compared with the base prices of T$130 million, T$120 million and T$120 million, respectively, the official said.
Securities analysts said this indicated an earlier-than-expected recovery in the construction and real estate market.

"Most analysts said they have seen bottoming-out effect in the real estate market and had forecast major recovery starting the latter half of 1997," said Oliver Fang, international sales head at National Securities.
"But the better-than-expected auction results signal that the expected recovery may come earlier," he said.
